title: Define banking rules and predicted examples
outcome: Write account creation, amount precision, Savings limit, Premium rule and transfer decisions.
checkpoint: Explain private balance, per-operation versus daily limits, and failure without mutation.
acceptance: Document at least six concrete success/failure examples; distinguish login user from bank account; explicitly defer interest if no rule.

title: Create account state and constructor
outcome: Implement the first BankAccount class yourself.
checkpoint: Which fields must be private? What makes an account valid at creation?
acceptance: Stable account ID; private BigDecimal balance; constructor rejects invalid state; no public balance setter.

title: Implement valid deposits
outcome: Add deposits with explicit validation.
checkpoint: What happens for null, zero, negative and excess-precision input?
acceptance: Valid decimal deposit updates correctly; invalid inputs leave state unchanged; predict and run both cases.

title: Implement withdrawals and insufficient funds handling
outcome: Enforce available-balance checks.
checkpoint: In which order should validation happen? Can the balance reach zero?
acceptance: Exact balance, overdraw, zero, negative and decimal amounts verified; rejection never changes balance.

title: Run a small console smoke demonstration
outcome: Write Main to demonstrate your existing operations.
checkpoint: Predict output before executing; keep banking logic outside Main.
acceptance: Compile and run com.vmargin.banking.Main; record actual versus predicted output; this is a development runner.

title: Write the first meaningful JUnit tests
outcome: Turn manual examples into repeatable tests.
checkpoint: What state before and after distinguishes correct behaviour from an accidental pass?
acceptance: Tests cover success and rejection; introduce a deliberate temporary mistake to show a test catches it, then restore correctly.

title: Implement justified Savings and Premium differences
outcome: Add agreed inheritance and overrides.
checkpoint: What rule changes between account types? Why is a cast unnecessary for overridden withdraw?
acceptance: Savings limit and sufficient balance both enforced; Premium still cannot overdraw; tests invoke through parent reference.

title: Introduce domain exceptions and caller handling
outcome: Give invalid operations clear failure signals.
checkpoint: How does throwing differ from printing an error? Which layer explains it to the user?
acceptance: Callers can distinguish relevant failures; no swallowed errors or partial mutation; tests assert exception and state.

title: Store and find multiple accounts behind a repository boundary
outcome: Add in-memory account lookup with a small contract.
checkpoint: Why might service code depend on a storage contract instead of a specific collection?
acceptance: Unique IDs; missing account handled; lookup tests; interface introduced only after learner explains it.

title: Record successful transaction history
outcome: Define records with amount, type, time and account identity.
checkpoint: Should callers be able to change old records? Which failures are recorded?
acceptance: History matches successful operations; rejected operations follow documented policy; order and decimal amounts verified.

title: Coordinate transfers between two accounts
outcome: Add transfer orchestration without duplicating account rules.
checkpoint: What if receiver lookup or validation fails after sender debit?
acceptance: Reject self and missing destination; preserve combined balance; no partial mutation on tested failures; two sides share a transfer reference.

title: Verify the domain gate and explain the design
outcome: Review the working core before Spring.
checkpoint: Trace one successful and one failed transfer without generated notes.
acceptance: Maven tests pass; important boundaries covered; author explains rules; document concurrency as unverified in-memory scope.

title: Choose UI and draw three simple screens
outcome: Commit to Thymeleaf default or explicitly budget React before UI implementation.
checkpoint: Is a separate browser app worth the second build and API work now?
acceptance: Dashboard, operation form and history sketch; error states; no commitment to rewriting Thymeleaf later.

title: Integrate Spring Boot around the tested domain
outcome: Select a supported Boot release then add only needed web dependencies.
checkpoint: What does Spring create and connect? Which rules remain ordinary Java?
acceptance: Core tests still pass; app starts; version compatibility verified; starter version pinned; domain rules not copied into controller.

title: Render dashboard and demo accounts
outcome: Display synthetic account balances in the selected UI.
checkpoint: Where does displayed state originate?
acceptance: Readable dashboard; balances from service; explicit demo/reset notice; no real personal data.

title: Create accounts through a form
outcome: Connect validated input to account creation.
checkpoint: How do browser validation and server validation differ?
acceptance: Valid account appears; blank or invalid input shows readable errors; stable ID generated; no direct field mutation.

title: Connect deposit and withdrawal forms
outcome: Expose existing operations through forms.
checkpoint: What happens when invalid text or an overdraw request reaches the server?
acceptance: Correct updated balance; readable rejected-operation errors; no changes on rejection; refresh does not repeat successful operation.

title: Display transfers and transaction history
outcome: Add complete transfer flow and history display.
checkpoint: How will the user know which two accounts changed?
acceptance: Both balances and history agree; unknown/self destination handled; success and failure verified end to end.

title: Style and verify keyboard-friendly pages
outcome: Apply Bootstrap and small deliberate styling.
checkpoint: Can a person find and correct an error without guessing?
acceptance: Visible labels, focus states, readable currency; desktop and narrow viewport checked; CSS assets available for submission.

title: Complete regression walkthrough and record limitations
outcome: Freeze optional features and verify the entire local app.
checkpoint: Which claims are supported by tests versus screenshots?
acceptance: Run build/tests; full happy and rejected flows; list unimplemented persistence/auth/deployment honestly.

title: Write README and practise technical explanation
outcome: Document actual setup, architecture and verified features.
checkpoint: Explain a rule change and the tests it affects.
acceptance: Fresh run instructions work; architecture and limitations match code; no fabricated hiring or security claims.

title: Capture screenshots and assemble submission PDF
outcome: Create screenshot documentation for September 12.
checkpoint: What does each image prove?
acceptance: Synthetic data consistent across screenshots; readable captions; PDF rendered and visually inspected; final upload remains user action.

title: Persist accounts and history in PostgreSQL
outcome: Add schema, repository implementation and environment configuration.
checkpoint: What changes when objects become rows? Why is H2 not required first?
acceptance: Data survives restart; SQL constraints and mappings tested; secrets external; migrations documented.

title: Verify database transfer atomicity and concurrency
outcome: Add database transaction boundary and lost-update protection.
checkpoint: What happens when two withdrawals race or a credit fails?
acceptance: Rollback and concurrent-withdrawal integration tests; choose explainable locking approach; no negative balance or partial transfer.

title: Implement authentication and account authorization
outcome: Add login only with explicit user-account ownership checks.
checkpoint: Authentication identifies who; authorization decides whose account they may act on.
acceptance: Password hashing via established library; session/CSRF design; another user's account access denied; credentials never committed.

title: Package with Docker if the selected host needs it
outcome: Create reproducible runtime packaging.
checkpoint: What persists outside a container and where does configuration come from?
acceptance: Image builds and app runs; no secrets in layers; ports and health check documented; optional independent of React/auth.

title: Deploy a bounded synthetic-data demo
outcome: Verify current free-host constraints and deploy when ready.
checkpoint: Is the demo isolated per session, resettable/shared, or authenticated?
acceptance: Explicit demo model chosen; ownership protected where needed; URL and full flows verified; persistence claims match deployment; cost/sleep limits documented.

title: Evaluate React as an optional frontend direction
outcome: Decide whether React adds justified learning value.
checkpoint: Which existing UI work would be replaced and what API contracts are needed?
acceptance: Decision records time cost; if accepted define separate issues for API, state, errors and build; no automatic rewrite.

title: Prepare interview demonstration from actual evidence
outcome: Build a concise demo and explainable resume claim.
checkpoint: Can you change a rule and repair its tests live?
acceptance: Explain domain, tests, framework and limitations; commit/test evidence tied to claims; no certificate inference from course badge.
